error.read_only: You cannot change `{object}.{name}` yourself. An action changes it.
error.not_called: `{name}` is an action. An action is done with brackets after it, like `{example}`.
error.unclosed: This line opens a `{what}` that never closes.
error.missing_colon: A line that starts with `{keyword}` ends with `:`.
error.indentation: The lines inside a `while`, an `if` or a `for` need four spaces in front.
error.arguments: `{name}` is not used like that. Try it like this: `{example}`.
error.no_such_module: There is no book called `{name}` in the school's library.
error.unknown_action: `{object}` does not know an action called `{name}`.
error.no_new_attribute: You cannot give `{object}` a new `{name}`. What `{object}` can do is in its notebook.
error.no_knot: This broom has no knot, so there is nothing to untie, and the program stops here. Before taking the knot off a broom, look whether it has one.
error.no_landing: There is nowhere to set the broom down here, so the program stops here, still in the air. Land where there is ground.
error.index_range: The list doesn't have that many: it has {count}, and you wanted number {asked}.
error.index_range_unknown: The list doesn't have as many as you asked for.
error.ring_rim: The broom turned while it was still inside the ring and rubbed its rim, so the program stops here, still in the air. Leave the ring by its other side, one step more upward or downward, before turning.

plan.title: The naughty child's map
plan.legend: A cell is two numbers: x counts from the left, y from the top, and both start at 0.

blocked.locked: I cannot open {thing}: it is locked, and I have no key for it.

blocked.nothing: There is nothing here to pick up.

blocked.sealed: I cannot open {thing} by hand: it is sealed, and needs a spell.

wizard.move_right: Walks right, one tile per step. Stops at a wall or a closed door.
wizard.move_left: Walks left, one tile per step. Stops at a wall or a closed door.
wizard.move_up: Walks up, one tile per step. Stops at a wall or a closed door.
wizard.move_down: Walks down, one tile per step. Stops at a wall or a closed door.
wizard.wait: Stands still while the world moves on, one tick at a time; wizard.wait(2) waits two.
wizard.pick_up: Picks up a thing on the wizard's tile or beside it, and carries it. With several in reach, say which: wizard.pick_up(key).
wizard.find_nearest: Finds the nearest thing of a kind, or None when there is none. Where a place has parts, like the shed's wall and its straw, it only finds those in the part where the wizard stands.
wizard.find_item: Finds the thing of a kind the wizard carries, or None when it carries none.
wizard.find_all: Finds every thing of a kind and gives them in a list, nearest first, even where something covers them: brooms = wizard.find_all("broom"); len(brooms) says how many. Where a place has parts, like the shed's wall and its straw, it only finds those in the part where the wizard stands.
wizard.has: Tells whether the wizard carries a thing of a kind.
wizard.position: The cell the wizard stands on, as x and y, counted from 0 from the left and from the top: print(wizard.position) shows it.
wizard.facing: The way the wizard looks: up, down, left or right.
wizard.items: The things the wizard carries, in a list; len(wizard.items) says how many.
wizard.cast: Casts a spell with the wand, which the wizard must carry. What a spell does depends on where the wizard stands and what is near; it may do nothing at all. The fendra spell is also given the thing to bring: wizard.cast("fendra", book). The orvim spell opens the map, when the wizard carries it: wizard.cast("orvim"). The drevo spell lifts the broom, when the wizard carries it, and sets it down again when cast in the air: wizard.cast("drevo").
wizard.give: Gives a thing the wizard carries to whoever stands right beside it.
wizard.sleep: Lies down and sleeps in a free bed.
wizard.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from the wizard to an object.
wizard.flying: True while the wizard flies on the broom, from the moment drevo lifts it until it lands.

thing.kind: What the thing is, like "key" or "book".
thing.name: The thing's own name in this level.
thing.position: The cell the thing lies on, as x and y, or None once the wizard carries it or while it lies in the dark.
thing.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
thing.reveal: Makes a thing glow where it lies, even through whatever hides it, so that you see where it is.

door.name: The door's own name in this level.
door.position: Where the door stands, as x and y.
door.locked: True while the door needs its key to open.
door.is_open: True once the door is open, and the wizard can go through.
door.open: Opens the door. The wizard must stand next to it, and carry its key if it is locked. A sealed door, or one with a password, does not open by hand.
door.sealed: True while the door is sealed, until its spell is cast beside it.
door.password: The word that opens the door when it is said beside it, or None.
door.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
door.reveal: Shows where a hidden thing lies.

key.name: The key's own name in this level.
key.position: The cell the key lies on, as x and y, or None once the wizard carries it or while it lies in the dark.
key.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
key.reveal: Shows where a hidden thing lies.

teacher.name: The teacher's own name in this level.
teacher.position: Where the teacher stands, as x and y.
teacher.facing: The way the teacher looks, as a string: "up", "down", "left" or "right", so that a program can look before each step: dask.facing == "up".
teacher.can_see: Tells whether the teacher can see something straight ahead, close enough.
teacher.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.

ghost.name: The ghost's name in this level.
ghost.position: Where the ghost floats, in x and y.
ghost.facing: The way the ghost looks: up, down, left or right.
ghost.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.

cat.name: The cat's name in this level.
cat.position: Where the cat sits, in x and y.
cat.facing: The way the cat looks: up, down, left or right.
cat.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.

hole.name: The hole's own name in this level.
hole.position: The cell of the hole, in x and y; on a hole of two cells, the first.
hole.open: True while the hole is open in the floor, so that a step onto it, taken now, cannot be taken; a program can wait for it to close: while hole.open.
hole.closed: True while the floor covers the hole, so that a step onto it, taken now, is safe; a program can wait for it: while not hole.closed.
hole.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
hole.reveal: Shows where a hidden thing lies.

position.x: A cell's first number, its column: how many cells from the left, counting from 0.
position.y: A cell's second number, its row: how many cells from the top, counting from 0.

bed.name: The bed's own name in this level.
bed.position: Where the bed stands, in x and y.
bed.free: True when no one sleeps in the bed.
bed.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
bed.reveal: Shows where a hidden thing lies.

broom.name: The broom's own name in this level.
broom.position: The cell the broom lies on, as x and y, or None once the wizard carries it.
broom.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.
broom.reveal: Makes a thing glow where it lies, even through whatever hides it, so that you see where it is.
broom.knotted: True while the black thread is knotted in the broom's twigs: if broom.knotted:
broom.untie: Unties the knot in the broom. The wizard must stand on it, and the broom must have a knot: if it has none, that is an error.

racer.name: The name of who races you in this level.
racer.position: Where the one racing you is, as x and y.
racer.facing: The way the one racing you looks: "up", "down", "left" or "right".
racer.distance_to: Gives the number of steps from an object to the wizard.

run.does: Runs your code. On a Mac, Cmd+Enter or Option+R.

notebook.does: Opens or closes the notebook. On a Mac, Option+N.

indent.does: Moves a line in by four spaces, or out again.

leave.does: Leaves the editor, so that Tab moves to the next button.

close.does: Closes a card over the scene.

split.does: On the handle between the scene and the editor, moves it.

wizard.title: Your wizard
wizard.name: Your wizard's name
wizard.name_rule: A name has letters, digits, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes, up to 20 of them.
wizard.name_taken: That name belongs to someone or something in the game. Choose another.
wizard.gender_first: Choose first who your wizard is, and their looks appear here.

wizard.move_right: Walks one step to the right.
wizard.move_left: Walks one step to the left.
wizard.wait: Stands still for one tick, while the world goes on.

notebook_python.len: Gives how many values a list has: len(brooms) is the number of brooms in the list brooms.
notebook_python.def: Gives a name to the lines moved in under it, a function. They run each time the name is written with brackets: quick_fly().
notebook_python.def_arguments: The names in the brackets of def are the function's arguments: the call gives them their values in the same order, two_rings(2, 4).

stars.kept: You keep the {n} stars you had.

spells.zelim: breaks the seal of a door beside you.
spells.fendra: brings to your cell the thing you name, three cells away at most in a straight line.
spells.kirra: lights the dark room you are in.
spells.osto: holds closed, for a while, a hole beside you that opens in the floor.
spells.orvim: opens the naughty child's map on the plan of the place you are in, every cell with its numbers, if you carry the map.
spells.drevo: lifts the broom you carry into the air: from then on your moves fly, three times as fast, over water, hedges and fences, but not through the crowns of trees or walls; cast it again in the air and the broom sets down, if the ground under it can be stood on; at the program's end the broom sets down by itself wherever there is ground.

words.ambrel: the school's word, which opens its gates.

race.reading: Ilda reads the programs: you, {mine} lines; {name}, {theirs}.
race.judged_wizard: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}, and therefore {wizard} has won.
race.judged_racer: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}, and therefore {name} has won.
race.judged_tie: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}. It is a tie! The race is flown again.
race.judged_penalty_racer: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}. But {wizard} had a penalty of {penalty} ticks, and therefore {name} has won.
race.judged_penalty_wizard: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}. {wizard} had a penalty of {penalty} ticks, but has won even so.
race.judged_penalty_tie: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}. But {wizard} had a penalty of {penalty} ticks, so with it they are tied. The race is flown again.
race.judged_slower: {wizard} took {own} ticks and {name} took {theirs}. In addition, {wizard} had a penalty of {penalty} ticks, and therefore {name} has won.
race.judged_unfinished: {wizard} did not cross the finish, and therefore {name} has won.

about.hero_alt: The castle of Arvelia on top of its hill by the lake at dusk, with the village at its foot
about.hero_text: You arrive at a school of magic, and every step you take there, you take by writing real programs.
about.what_text: Kydux is a game for learning to program in Python. Your character arrives at Arvelia, a school of magic in an old castle. There, everything obeys written instructions. To open a door, cross a corridor or fly on a broom, you write real Python.
about.who_text: For girls and boys from eight years old. No one needs to know how to program: the game teaches it step by step, one idea at a time. A grown-up can play alongside, and will learn too.
about.story_text: The challenges are set in a story full of intrigue and adventure that will hook you from the first day.
about.story_alt: A story: the characters at the broom shed, and the voice's words under them
about.lesson_text: You will learn how to write the programs with short lessons that explain the basic ideas of programming and of Python.
about.lesson_alt: A lesson: a page that explains lists, with its example
about.level_text: Kydux is a wizard newly arrived at the school of magic. You will face different challenges, and you will solve each by writing small programs that control the character.
about.level_alt: A level: the scene on the left and the program on the right
about.free_title: Free, and of the Kidux family
about.free_text: Kydux is free software, under the GNU General Public License. It is in English and in Spanish, and it is played in a web browser. It belongs to the Kidux family, a system for a child's first computer.

tips.notebook: Open the notebook to see all the instructions you can use in your program.
tips.spells: In the notebook, you can also see all the available spells and magic words.
tips.click: If you click on an instruction in the notebook, it writes itself into your program.
tips.dot: If you type an object's name followed by a dot, all the things that object has will appear so you don't have to type them.
tips.hint: When your program doesn't win, you can press the *Hint* button under the program. Each press shows one more hint, up to three!
tips.keys: To run your program, press Ctrl+Enter or Alt+R (Cmd+Enter or Option+R on a Mac). And with Alt+N (Option+N on a Mac) you can open and close the notebook.
tips.timeline: After running a program, you can drag the bar under the scene to go over what happened moment by moment and find out what went wrong.
tips.zoom: Use the *+* and *−* buttons (or the mouse wheel) to bring the scene nearer or farther. If you lose sight of your wizard, the *Find my wizard* button brings them back into view.
tips.lesson: In a lesson with an example of code, you can change it and press the *Run* button under it to see right there what your change does.
tips.map: The *Map* button opens the map. From there you can open again any stop you have already reached, to play it once more, and see the stars of every level you have won.
